The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiographic appearances of noncalcified breast malignancies are not specific for a given type of cancer.
the mammographic appearance of noncalcified cancers can vary considerably, and that this variability is related to tumor size, histologic type, and the histologic features at the margin of the tumor.
there is no single radiographic appearance that correlates with a specific histologic margin or histologic subtype.
